# Terminology and domain conventions

<!-- Generated by skill `init-dsh-project` v1.8 on 2026-10-26.
     DSH side: the glossary lives at the repo root in `CONTEXT.md` (for agents that consume this
     repo as a tool); this file says how to use it. -->

> Why this page exists: in this domain **the same word means different things in different
> sources** (the official contract, some reproduction project, our own implementation each call
> it something else). Leave the words unpinned and issue titles and test names talk past each
> other — and then the same bug gets filed twice.

## 1. Which word lives where

| Layer | File | Who reads it |
|---|---|---|
| This repo's vocabulary (nouns, abbreviations, coordinates) | repo root [`CONTEXT.md`](../CONTEXT.md) | people / agents using this repo as a tool |
| This repo's domain conventions (naming, citation, provenance) | this file | people changing this repo |
| Settled decisions | [`../adr/`](../adr/README.md) | anyone about to overturn a practice |

## 2. Naming conventions

| Thing | Rule | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Device ids | `D-<short>` in SOT / issues; full model + firmware in `CONTEXT.md` | `D-PC` (MateBook Pro S, MOR-M1), `D-X5` |
| Metric ids | `M<n>` in the epic SOT; never renumbered once frozen | `M3` frame pacing |
| Code branches (upstream-bound) | `hmos/<issue>-<slug>`, cut from `upstream/main` | `hmos/004-pc-2in1` |
| Play build branch | `hmos/integration` = upstream + open PR branches; never merged to `main` | — |
| Our commit scope | `harmony` / `docs` / `epic` / `tools`, issue id in the subject | `docs(epic): baseline M3 on D-X5 (#007)` |
| Device evidence files | outside git (scratchpad / host Documents); the issue quotes the numbers and the command | — |
| Shell strings | upstream's key style in `dm/i18n/ui_text.tsv`; never a literal in ArkTS | `dmAndroidImporting` |

## 3. Citation discipline (**where cross-source work goes wrong most often**)

Every number / conclusion carries exactly one tag:

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `(measured)` | Actually run on this machine or our device; attach the command, device id, firmware and build |
| `(official)` | Verbatim from first-party docs; attach file and line |
| `(author-reported)` / `(upstream-reported)` | Claimed by someone else's repo or paper — here usually upstream's docs — **not verified by us on our devices** |
| `(unverified)` | Explicitly not found or not run |

An untagged number does not enter an issue's Exit, an ADR's consequences, or a report.

## 4. When output contradicts an ADR

Say it out loud, never overwrite silently: state in the body "this contradicts ADR-XXXX,
because …", then either change the output or narrow the old decision with a new ADR.
**A silent inconsistency costs more than an error** — it makes the next person believe both.
